subject: MissionPay - SLA risk: throughput drop & elevated error rate from reserved pool
messages:
From: Sara Kim <sara.kim@missionpay.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: infra@missionpay.com
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: Urgent: sustained 5xx + throughput degradation from our reserved pool

Rishi —

We're seeing a platform-wide impact for MissionPay starting ~07:55 PST. Key observations: 
- 5xx error rate spiked to 4.6% across token-generation endpoints (historical baseline ~0.02%).
- p95 latency jumped to 1.8s (was ~380ms), p99 to 3.2s.
- Our committed reserved throughput on the Redwood Dedicated pool is delivering ~78% of target for the last 45m.

This is hitting our checkout flows (high QPS window) and we are starting to see downstream retries. We are scheduled to go live with a merchant on Monday; this is blocking.

I attached a short set of traces and a CSV of the rolling metrics. Can you confirm whether this is a pure capacity issue (pool saturation) or if there's a model-level regression? We need immediate mitigation and an ETA for resolution.

Sara Kim
Head of Platform — MissionPay
Sara.Kim@missionpay.com

Attachments: missionpay_sample_traces_20261210.log (12MB), metrics-snapshot-2026-12-10.csv (180KB)
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@missionpay.com>
Cc: naomi.feldman@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 08:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Urgent: sustained 5xx + throughput degradation from our reserved pool

Sara — thanks for the data and the heads up. I'm opening an incident and pulling in infra/ops now.

Immediate asks: can you share 3 example request IDs from the 08:00–08:10 window and confirm whether any recent model pins/rollouts were applied from your side in the last 6 hours?

Initial plan:
- Infra to validate whether Dedicated pool is at headroom and whether autoscaler triggered.
- Engineering (Olga) to look for kernel / memory / KV-cache pressure or recent model changes.
- Naomi / CS to coordinate customer comms.

I'll keep you looped every 15–30m. If we need to, we'll temporarily route traffic to a compatible hosted variant while we remediate.

—Rishi
Director, Customer Success (Escalations)
Redwood Inference
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MissionPay - initial triage notes (pool topology + quick mitigations)

Triage notes (quick):
- Observed: Dedicated pool for MissionPay (pool-id: dp-3057) reporting sustained GPU util ~96% across 8 nodes, large KV-cache growth and token generation latency correlation.
- Autoscaler status: did NOT trigger additional nodes. Our autoscaler saw short-lived spike then collapse — looks like a mis-evaluation from the occupancy heuristic when many long-sequence requests arrived concurrently.
- Notable: two model variants were pinned in the last 2 hours (v4.2-fp16 and v4.2-qat) — this caused fragmentation: some requests land on heavily-loaded nodes that did not have the quantized kernels warm. The runtime fell back to slower execution paths and caused queueing.

Immediate mitigations (executed now):
1) Temporary pool scale: requested +2 nodes (provisioning) — expected to be available in ~6–9m.
2) Traffic slicing: added an aggressive routing rule to steer 30% of MissionPay traffic to a hosted-compatible variant (latency tradeoff small, avoids hitting committed SLA for reserved).
3) Kernel warm-up: pushed a background warm-up job for the QAT variant to pre-load quantized kernels on idle nodes.
4) If provisioning doesn't increase headroom in 12m, recommend rolling back the recent pin for v4.2-qat to v4.2-fp16-only to reduce fragmentation.

I'm attaching a metrics snapshot and the pool topology screenshot. I'll follow up with a short post-mortem once stabilized.

—Olga
Sr. Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: pool-topology-annotated.png; metrics-snapshot-2026-12-10.csv
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@missionpay.com>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: priyom.das@redwood.com, olga.petrov@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 08:55:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MissionPay - customer comms plan and short-term remediation

Sara — quick update and proposed customer communication: 
- What we did: added two nodes, implemented temporary 30% reroute to hosted variant, started kernel warm-up. Initial telemetry shows error rate down from 4.6% → 0.9% in the last 8 minutes and p95 latency improving (now ~860ms).
- Next 60m plan: monitor headroom; if autoscaler still underfills, we'll authorize an extra +2 nodes (exec-approved until EOD) and run a controlled rollback of the recent pin if required.
- Customer ask: do you approve the temporary 30% reroute to hosted? This will preserve committed capacity for other traffic and prevent checkout failures while we fully remediate.

We will offer a one-time credit for the impacted hour window and provide an incident summary by EOD. Proposed post-mortem call: 12/11 09:30 PST.

Naomi Feldman
Head of Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, naomi.feldman@redwood.com, olga.petrov@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 10 Dec 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MissionPay - SLA risk: throughput drop & elevated error rate from reserved pool

Thanks team — quick executive note:
- Impact: mission-critical merchant rollouts are at risk; remediation is priority.
- Authorization: approve temporary capacity (additional nodes) and the hosted-reroute for up to 24 hours. Finance is ok with a discretionary credit if CS recommends.
- Ask to Rishi/Naomi: please prepare a 3-bullet executive summary for the MissionPay CTO and our C-levels summarizing root cause, actions taken, and expected timeline. Send to me and I'll join the 09:30 PST call if helpful.

Marcus Lin
VP Sales & GTM, Redwood Inference
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sara Kim <sara.kim@missionpay.com>
Cc: naomi.feldman@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, olga.petrov@redwood.com, priyom.das@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 09:45:00 -0800
Subject: MissionPay incident update — stabilization and next steps

Sara — final update and next steps after today's remediation: 
- Status: pool headroom restored; error rate returned to baseline (~0.03%) and p95 latency stabilized ~420ms by 09:15 PST. The temporary hosted-reroute was removed at 08:50 PST.
- Root cause (preliminary): autoscaler heuristic under-reacted to long-sequence bursts combined with a recent model-variant pin that introduced kernel warming variance.
- Actions taken: +2 nodes provisioned, kernel warm-up executed, short-lived routing to hosted variant, and we scheduled an autoscaler-heuristic patch (ETA 48h) plus a process change to require runtime warm-up for new pins.
- Customer remediation: we will provide a one-hour usage credit for the impacted window and deliver a written post-mortem by EOD. Post-mortem call confirmed for 12/11 09:30 PST (invite sent).

Links: Incident: https://redwood.pagerduty.com/incidents/PD-129874; Post-mortem draft: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/missionpay-2026-12-10

Thanks for patience and flagging this early — will follow up with the PM/ops post-mortem.

—Rishi
Director, Customer Success (Escalations)
Redwood Inference
